reader_question: How has the law changed the child tax credit’s top amount per child since 2017?
grade_line: Documented: public laws and an IRS revenue procedure
title: Congress has changed the child tax credit’s top amount per child three times since 2017: to $2,000 in 2018, $3,000 for 2021 alone and $2,200 from 2025.
reading_guide: Each flat run is a tax year, or a run of years, when one amount held. The line steps up or down in the year a law changed the amount.
measure_line: Top amount of the child tax credit per qualifying child, dollars, tax years 2017 to 2026, United States, before income limits and refundability caps. The chart starts in 2017, the last year before Public Law 115-97 doubled the amount. The scale starts at zero.
notes: Public Law 115-97, signed December 22, 2017, set $2,000 per child for 2018 through 2025.

Public Law 117-2, signed March 11, 2021, set $3,000 per child for 2021 alone, $3,600 for a child under 6, and made the credit fully refundable that year. Those rules then lapsed, and 2022 went back to $2,000.

Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025, set $2,200 from 2025, made the amount permanent and tied it to inflation. The yearly adjustment rounds down to a multiple of $100, so 2026 stays at $2,200 (IRS Revenue Procedure 2025-32).
Few families get exactly the top amount: income limits, phase-outs, the cap on the refundable part ($1,700 for 2025 and 2026) and, from 2025, Social Security number rules set each family’s credit.
alt: Step line of the child tax credit’s top amount per child, tax years 2017 to 2026: $1,000 in 2017, $2,000 from 2018 to 2020, $3,000 in 2021 ($3,600 for a child under 6), $2,000 again from 2022 to 2024, and $2,200 in 2025 and 2026.

Labels on the line: Public Law 115-97 at 2018, Public Law 117-2 at 2021, the 2021 rules lapsing at 2022 and Public Law 119-21 at 2025.
